absent: Full layouts of buffer descriptors, folios, address spaces, block devices, bios and writeback control beyond fields referenced here.
Semantics of block layer dispatch, device end guarding, crypto submission and IO completion beyond association described.
Slow lookup path, access marking, cache disable control and folio cache acquisition beyond call sites shown.
Dirty and writeback infrastructure including folio marking helpers, inode dirty flags and backing writeback identity assignment.
Journal buffer creation, block size helpers and device capacity retrieval beyond capacity bound use.
Implementations of locking, atomic, percpu, scheduling, bug check and logging primitives owned by other dossiers.

findings.text: Block buffer acquisition and read services are available for block devices by block number and size, covering cache lookup with allocation, synchronous read that ensures validity, and opportunistic readahead that releases its reference promptly.

Dirtying, writeback accounting and boundary flushing services are available, covering single buffer marking, folio wide marking, metadata association handling, cgroup ownership attribution and flushing of a trailing boundary block.

Buffer descriptor and folio attachment lifecycle services are available, covering descriptor allocation and release, per folio chain creation for pages and folios, data pointer establishment, empty chain creation with initial state, invalidation over ranges, and reclamation attempts.

Per processor cache maintenance and reference helpers are available, covering global and local cache draining, presence probing, reference release with null tolerance, count decrement with ordering, and sleepable lock and wait operations with nonblocking attempts.

Submission expects a buffer that is already locked and mapped and that carries neither delay nor unwritten indication; a rewrite clears a prior write error indication exactly once per request marking, while metadata and priority attributes widen the operation flags.

Submission IO is addressed by scaling the block number with the buffer size relative to sector units, carries the caller write hint, binds completion handling and private context back to the originating buffer, is constrained at device end, and when writeback control is present is associated with it including cgroup attribution before crypto aware dispatch.

Crypto association is skipped when the folio has no address space mapping, which covers directly created journal buffers outside page cache; otherwise the host inode and byte position derived from folio start plus buffer offset are used, and in the routed configuration the downstream helper performs no action.

Cgroup ownership accounting is inactive without backing writeback state or when explicitly disabled, ignores offline groups, accumulates bytes directly on identity match, separately tracks a leading candidate, and maintains a trailing candidate through incremental majority vote dynamics that reset when empty.

Buffer cache lookup first consults a per processor small residency set with move to front promotion on hit and reference acquisition, falling back to a slow path that marks access and installs on success; installation rotates the set, retains residency with an extra reference, and releases the displaced entry.

Folio buffer chains are built with uniform size and descending offsets, initialized to unmapped block identity, linked circularly and attached privately to the folio; initialization numbers blocks from the folio file position, propagates folio validity, and marks mapped status only for blocks strictly inside device capacity.

Device folio growth reuses compatible attached buffers when sizes match, otherwise attempts reclamation and signals retry on failure, allocates fresh chains with accounted memory under private exclusion, and reports whether the requested block lies within capacity; outer sizing rejects overflowing or excessively large requests and validates alignment of size against logical block size.

Single buffer dirtying warns when validity is absent, uses an ordered double check to fast path the already dirty case, and on transition propagates dirtiness from buffer to folio to host inode exactly once; folio wide dirtying marks every attached descriptor under private exclusion before folio and inode propagation and reports whether the folio newly became dirty.

Metadata dirtying additionally claims association with a supplied collection exactly once through atomic installation and queue transfer, tolerating duplicate claims from corrupted multiply claimed blocks without list corruption; collection invalidation drains all associated entries under exclusion.

Range invalidation requires a locked folio and a non overflowing window, discards only fully covered buffers while stopping before partial overlap, releases private data only when the whole folio is covered, and always clears the mapped to disk indication; discarding detaches device association, clears dirtiness and mapping related state atomically under buffer exclusion.

A buffer is considered busy when its reference count is nonzero or when dirty or locked indications are present; reclamation detaches private linkage only after verifying every descriptor is idle and removing association queues, then frees the detached chain outside exclusion, and cleans folio dirtiness when reclamation succeeds under mapping exclusion.

Synchronous slow read serializes on the buffer, returns immediately when already valid, otherwise issues a read and waits, succeeding only when validity is achieved and otherwise releasing the reference and reporting absence; readahead and outer read wrappers acquire cache entries with blocking tolerance matched allocation modes and enforce no fail allocation with filesystem constrained flags.

Global buffer head pressure is estimated by rate limited aggregation of per processor counts, sampling at most once per several thousand accounting events and setting an over limit indication when the total exceeds a configured maximum.
Boundary maintenance inspects the block immediately following a given block without blocking, issues a write for it only when dirty, and always drops the lookup reference.

Buffer locking is sleepable and uses a fast nonblocking attempt with blocking fallback, while waiting likewise may sleep and only blocks when the locked indication is present; conditional readahead proceeds only when validity is absent and the nonblocking attempt succeeds.

Per processor residency sets are guarded by either interrupt exclusion or preemption exclusion depending on configuration, require interrupts to be enabled on entry, and are bypassed entirely on isolated processors or when the cache is administratively disabled.

Mapping private exclusion serializes folio buffer list attachment, initialization, folio wide dirty marking, reclamation and empty chain publication against concurrent lookup and dirty paths, preserving dirty bit coherence and atomicity of chain linkage.

Descriptor allocation initializes association linkage and validity exclusion, while metadata collection exclusion serializes association claiming and draining; buffer exclusion serializes discard updates and slow read checks.
The per processor residency structure holds a fixed length array of buffer descriptor pointers with capacity defined centrally, instantiated once per processor with all entries initially empty.

Folio buffer chains use circular linkage across descriptors of equal size, each descriptor referencing its folio and a data address that encodes the intra folio offset directly for high memory and as a folio base plus offset otherwise.

Acquisition moves from residency hit to reuse, otherwise to folio growth and slow lookup with retry until an entry is obtained or growth fails; initialization assigns sequential block identities and mapped status bounded by device capacity.

Submission state requires locked and mapped standing, records request initiation to gate error clearing, and binds IO completion back to the buffer with device end protection and optional writeback association before dispatch.

Dirty lifecycle advances from validity to buffer dirtiness to folio dirtiness to inode dirtiness, with idempotent re marking and folio wide batch marking; invalidation reverses mapping related state and optionally detaches private linkage for full coverage.

Residency lifecycle installs newly found entries at the front with rotation and reference retention, promotes hits to the front, and drains entries globally across processors or locally on the current processor with reference release.

Primary block access entries accept device, block number, size and allocation mode to obtain cache entries, perform synchronous reads ensuring validity, trigger nonblocking readahead, and flush a following boundary block when dirty.
Folio oriented entries operate on address space and folio to mark dirtiness, invalidate ranges with folio locking, and establish empty buffer chains with caller supplied initial state.

Releasing a descriptor with zero references, freeing with nonempty association linkage, invalidating with overflowing ranges, establishing data beyond folio size, requesting unaligned sizes or out of range blocks each trigger warnings or errors and fail the operation rather than proceeding.

Reclamation must not proceed for unlocked folios, folios under writeback, or chains with referenced, dirty or locked members; forgetting clears dirtiness and association before release, while reference decrement enforces ordering before atomic update.

Residency retention pins attached folios against reclamation and migration, so installation is skipped while migration sensitive caching is disabled and lookup and installation are bypassed on isolated processors.
Per processor buffer residency capacity is sixteen entries.
Discard clears the set of mapped, new, request, delay and unwritten indications.
